newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARCELONA AND BETIS LOOK AHEAD WITH OPTIMISM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARCELONA AND BETIS LOOK AHEAD WITH OPTIMISM.

text.p: Both the winners and the losers of the Spanish Cup final on Saturday night are already aiming to improve on this season's efforts.
Barcelona beat Real Betis 3-2 after extra time in the Santiago Berbabeu stadium in Madrid but lifting the Cup is just the start of their ambitions, not the end.
Club president Jose Luis Nunez said: "I hope we are all here this time next year to celebrate winning the European Cup."
Barcelona last won the European Cup in 1992 but have gained entry to next year's Champions League by finishing second in the Spanish league.
After a year in which they won the Spanish Cup, the Spanish Supercup and the European Cup Winners' Cup, only the league title eluded them.
Spanish international defender Miguel Angel Nadal, who missed the final through injury, believes Barcelona will soon fill in the gaps in their trophy cabinet.
"Next season we'll certainly take the league and the European Cup," he said.
Almost all their squad have international pedigree. Nevertheless Nunez has given new coach Louis van Gaal the mandate and the money to spend on some team rebuilding.
A goalkeeper and new right-sided defender may be top of his shopping list after an indifferent final from Vitor Baia and Albert Ferrer.
More firepower may also be required if the departures of the Brazilian pair of Ronaldo and Giovanni are confirmed.
However, despite rumours that he was likely to follow Ronaldo to an Italian club, captain Josep Guardiola is now talking about staying at Barcelona.
Betis can feel equally optimistic. They are hoping that next season will bring their first major honour since they won the Spanish cup in 1977.
The Seville club will play in the Cup Winners' Cup next season as Barcelona are in the Champions League.

Betis will also look to make more of an impact on the domestic scene. They briefly topped the league last September but hopes of winning the title for the first time since 1935 faded as the season wore on.

However, with Nigerian international Finidi George back to full fitness and with such talents as striker Alfonso Munoz and their Croatian midfielder Robert Jarni committed to the club, Betis may also be in with a chance of taking the plaudits from the likes of Barcelona and reigning champions Real Madrid.
